stem.en: Which part of Dalton's theory explains the Law of Conservation of Mass?

text.en: Atoms are not created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. They only rearrange, so the total mass cannot change.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios, so the mass stays the same.
Atoms of different elements have different masses, so the totals always match.

explanation.en: If every atom that goes into a reaction comes out of it, the total mass before and after must be the same. Option b explains why compounds have fixed ratios, not why the total stays the same. Option c is true, but different masses alone tell you nothing about the total before and after.

hints.en: This law is about the total before and after. Which postulate says that nothing is lost or gained?
